title: Canonical constant-tower interchange and cochain localization unit
statement:
Let $A,B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with ordinary unbounded derived categories and localization functors $Q_A,Q_B$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], in independently chosen localization universes. Put $T=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, let $\operatorname{Tow}(A)=\operatorname{Fun}(T,A)$ and similarly for $B$ [def-weil-inverse-system], and let $\Delta_A,\Delta_B$ be the constant-tower functors. For an additive exact functor $F:B\to A$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive], assuming these four derived categories exist, define the constant interchange
$$D(F^{\operatorname{Tow}})\circ D(\Delta_B)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(\Delta_A)\circ D(F)$$
to be the composite of the inverse exact-derived composition comparison for $(\Delta_B,F^{\operatorname{Tow}})$, the exact localization of the identity-component ordinary isomorphism $F^{\operatorname{Tow}}\circ\Delta_B\cong\Delta_A\circ F$, and the exact-derived composition comparison for $(F,\Delta_A)$. Here $F^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ applies $F$ levelwise, and $D$ of an exact functor means its canonical localization. For an additive functor $G:A\to B$, assuming $A$ has K-injective resolutions, use the canonical total right derived functor $RG$ and its homotopy-level universal unit [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Define its cochain unit at every complex $I$ as the actual composite
$$Q_B(GI)\longrightarrow Q^h_B(q_B(GI))\longrightarrow Q^h_B(G_K(q_A I))\longrightarrow RG(Q^h_A(q_A I))\longrightarrow RG(Q_A I).$$
Here $q_A,q_B$ are the quotients from complexes to homotopy categories and $Q^h_A,Q^h_B$ their derived localizations; the first arrow is the inverse quotient/localization factorization isomorphism, the second is $Q^h_B$ applied to the inverse factorization of the degreewise functor through homotopy, the third is the homotopy-level unit of $RG$, and the last is $RG$ applied to the quotient/localization factorization isomorphism. These are definitions of specified maps, without an assertion about their compatibility with adjunction transposes.
